# AI goal types

<!-- Generated by `coney-tools refs render` from research/references/goal-types.yaml. Do not edit. -->

Every goal class a brain can have on its goal stack, by the type id the class reports, with the script
bindings that push it ([AI: goals](../research/ai.md#goals), [AI bindings](bindings/ai.md)). A goal binding's
callback is called 33 ms after the goal ends with the human's handle and whether the goal completed
([scripted goals](../research/ai.md#scripted)).

!!! info "What is complete"

    All 149 goal classes are listed, read from their vtables in the executable: type ids 0-158, with 10, 30,
    76, 77, 81, 97, 98, 106, 139 and 151 unused. 67 have a binding that makes them (found by following each binding's
    code three calls deep); the others are pushed by the game's own AI. What a goal does is written only where the
    [AI](../research/ai.md) page traces it; the class names are the game's.

149 entries. Data: `research/references/goal-types.yaml`.

## Sources and evidence

Evidence levels used: confirmed-code.

- SLUS_212.15, goal vtables (type +0x0c, name +0x14) and the bindings' code

## Fields

| Field | Type | Hand-written | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | int | | The goal type: what the class's type function returns (vtable `+0x0c`). |
| `name` | str | | The class's own name (the string vtable `+0x14` returns). |
| `vtable` | hex | | The class's vtable. |
| `process` | hex | | Its Process function (vtable `+0x44`), run each brain update. |
| `event` | hex | | Its own event handler (vtable `+0x4c`), when it has one. |
| `bindings` | list | | The script bindings that make it (found by following their code). |
| `calls` | int | | Script calls of those bindings. |
| `scripts` | list | | The scripts that make those calls (at most six). |
| `meaning` | str | yes | What the goal does, in our words. |
| `source` | str | yes | Where the entry comes from: a script and binding, an address, a chunk. |
| `evidence` | str | yes | How we know: confirmed-code, confirmed-runtime, inferred or speculative ([evidence levels](../guides/research-workflow.md#evidence-levels)). |
| `notes` | str | yes | Our own short notes. |
